<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel Boost guidelines curated by Laravel maintainers for this application; follow closely. This is a Laravel app using: laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12, laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0, laravel/mcp (MCP) v0, laravel/pint (PINT) v1, laravel/sail (SAIL) v1, phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v11. Abide by existing code conventions and application structure: follow sibling file structure; use descriptive names (e.g. `isRegisteredForDiscounts`); check existing components before writing new ones; stick to existing directory structure (don't create new base folders without approval); do not change application's dependencies without approval; do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works (unit/feature tests more important); be concise in explanations; only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user.
If user doesn't see a frontend change reflected in the UI, it could mean they need `bun run build`, `bun run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them.
Laravel Boost is an MCP server with powerful tools designed for this application—use them. Use `list-artisan-commands` to double check available Artisan command parameters. Use `get-absolute-url` for any project URL. Use `tinker` for PHP debugging or direct Eloquent queries. Use `database-query` when only reading from DB. Use `browser-logs` for recent browser logs/errors/exceptions (ignore old logs). Use `search-docs` before other approaches for Laravel-ecosystem docs (it passes installed packages/versions to remote API); pass array of packages to filter when needed. Use multiple broad, simple, topic-based queries first (e.g. `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`). Do not add package names to queries (package info already provided); use examples: 1) query=authentication 2) query=rate limit 3) query="infinite scroll" 4) query=middleware "rate limit" - "middleware" AND exact phrase "rate limit" 5) Multiple Queries query=["authentication","middleware"] (ANY). Search the documentation before making code changes.
Formatting/usage requirements: Always use curly braces for control structures, even if it has one line. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()` (e.g. `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`). Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods and functions. Use appropriate PHP type hints for method parameters. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments; never use comments within code unless _very_ complex. Add useful array shape type definitions for arrays when appropriate. Typically, keys in an Enum should be TitleCase. Example rule: `FavoritePerson`, `BestLake`, `Monthly`.
=== laravel/core rules ===
Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (migrations, controllers, models, etc.); can list commands with `list-artisan-commands`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands; pass correct `--options` for behavior. If creating a generic PHP class, use `php artisan make:class`. Always use proper Eloquent relationship methods with return type hints; prefer relationships over raw queries/manual joins. Use Eloquent models/relationships before raw DB queries; avoid `DB::`; prefer `Model::query()`; generate code that prevents N+1 via eager loading; use query builder for very complex DB operations. When creating new models, create useful factories and seeders too; ask user if they need other things, using `list-artisan-commands` to check available options to `php artisan make:model`. For APIs, default to Eloquent API Resources and API versioning unless existing API routes do not—then follow existing app convention. Always create Form Request classes for validation rather than inline validation in controllers; include both validation rules and custom error messages; check sibling Form Requests for array vs string based validation rules. Use queued jobs for time-consuming operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use Laravel built-in authentication/authorization features (gates, policies, Sanctum, etc.). When linking to other pages, prefer named routes and `route()`. Use environment variables only in configuration files—never use `env()` outside config; always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. For tests/models, use factories; check factory custom states before manually setting up model. Faker: use `$this->faker->word()`/`fake()->randomDigit()` following existing conventions. When creating tests, use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; pass `--unit` for unit tests; most tests should be feature tests. If you receive `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest`, you can run `bun run build` or ask user to run `bun run dev` or `composer run dev`. Use `search-docs` for version-specific documentation. Since Laravel 11, this project uses streamlined file structure: No middleware files in `app/Http/Middleware/`; `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware/exceptions/routing files; `bootstrap/providers.php` contains app specific service providers; **No app\Console\Kernel.php**—use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php` for console configuration. Commands auto-register: files in `app/Console/Commands/` are automatically available. When modifying a column, migration must include all previously defined column attributes or they will be dropped/lost. Laravel 11 supports limiting eagerly loaded records natively without external packages: `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Casts should be set in `casts()` method rather than `$casts` property; follow existing conventions.
=== pint/core rules ===
